finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws. The result is discarded, so the OWNER check is never enforced. Any caller can wipe any tenant. The sibling export() uses checkRole(), which throws, so it is not affected.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (with no OWNER role) sending POST /tenants/{t}/wipe with an arbitrary tenant id
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant), a destructive wipe of tenant data

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) is the handler for POST /tenants/{t}/wipe. Both arguments come from the request.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") is called as a statement and its boolean result is ignored.
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and never throws, as its Javadoc says.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard on the path is requireRole at line 26, and it has no effect because the return value is unused. No other authentication or authorization layer or tenant-ownership check exists in the codebase. checkRole (lines 18-22) would throw correctly but is not used here. export() at line 32 uses checkRole, so it is correctly guarded.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole at src/Admin.java:26 returns a boolean and its result is discarded. No other filter, interceptor or tenant check exists in the codebase.
